passages: SKL-S07: complete NPS page, contract/tooling paragraphs and dated 1822/1832 testimony
SKL-S06: printed p.55, PDF p.89, note225
claims.entailment: Patent 1811, contract 1819 and subsequent tooling are separate events; prior musket-factory piecework and 55 occupations are documented. Claim does not turn managerial testimony into measured worker or cost gains.
claims.rival: Established task division predates Hall; machine implementation still needs skilled tooling. Test properly descriptive.
claims.lineage: S06 and S07 overlap through Smith-family scholarship; quotations not independently checked against archival originals.

passages: SKL-S06: printed p.59, PDF p.93, notes244–245 and figure19
claims.entailment: Working-gauge comparison to a separate reference set is explicit. Later physical Model 1841 inspection set supports equipment existence, not 1823 adoption or conformity of all output.
claims.rival: Machines alone versus operational metrology: reference checking supports a concrete task role but does not estimate incremental yield or cost. Frozen test is already underdetermined.
claims.lineage: Museum record and figure19 depict the same surviving set; gauge history is inherited through Smith 1977, not independent archaeological replication.

passages: SKL-S08: printed pp.118–121, especially120 (PDF135); notes141–142 on printed335 (PDF350)
claims.entailment: Personal wrenches and salvaged tools provide task options; Katigiro narrates under-tree shop 1967 and larger site/welding 1972. Dates and scope match.
claims.rival: Demand, skill, customers and tools coevolve; narrative says business grew before investment. No exogenous tool access or apprentice cohort is observed. Frozen test is underdetermined and no earnings effect is claimed.
claims.lineage: Retrospective named interviews in 2011–12 plus author apprenticeship; no independent career-panel replication.

passages: SKL-S11: publisher footnotes 2,8,10,11; main body restricted
claims.entailment: Simultaneous changes prevent separate input attribution; teaching burden and at least six power-unit failures by June 1975 support material/time alternatives to a communication-only account. Footnote 10 specifies roughly two weeks delay on three occasions, not total delay allocation.
claims.rival: Learning may itself affect hardware reliability; observed failures do not prove an exogenous hardware effect. Frozen test is underdetermined.
claims.lineage: Coauthored builder follow-up within Collins research programme; not independent theory confirmation.

claims.entailment: Late offer +9–10 percentage points is not significant; early-versus-late contrast p=.08. Choice-of-timing use does not follow one simple-model prediction. These are offer/use comparisons, while earlier pilot data measure purchases.
claims.rival: Seasonal resources, fixed costs and advance announcement share predictions with present bias. Maize-sale and announced-delay tests constrain some simple variants but do not independently identify a discount parameter.
claims.lineage: Same SAFI programme/team; demonstration-plot pilot farmers differ from main sample and cannot be treated as independent population replication.

passages: PSY-S03: Table II printed 1330 (PDF 20), adjacent pp.1329–1331; §III measurement design
claims.entailment: Baseline 489 denominator, 86% current pod-size and 87% optimal-size nonresponse exactly match; spacing answers and enumerator measurements are distinguished.
claims.rival: Answering in grams may reflect measurement vocabulary as well as attention. Claim is descriptive and acknowledges that limitation.
claims.lineage: One original seaweed experiment; baseline elicitation precedes intervention outcomes, and 2012/2014 versions are one lineage.

passages: PSY-S11: §§3.2–3.3 printed8–10, §4.4.2 printed15–16, Appendix B printed74–75
PSY-S14: complete primary Oxford abstract returned by search, direct article open failed
claims.entailment: One-way minutes and prior-week absent days match;35.08/103.77=33.8055% and.29/1.01=28.7129%. N 1,879 and 1,952 are outcome-specific respondent counts; 100 schools,25/20/55 allocation match. Package includes mechanics/custody.
claims.rival: School randomisation supports total-package reported-outcome effect relative to common trends; attrition/self-report and mediation remain limited. No bare-asset or independent repair effect follows.
claims.lineage: Manuscript and final abstract are one 2017–18 Zambia experiment, with later administrative collection separately dated.

passages: PSY-S11: Table 3 printed40 (PDF41), Table A.11 printed56 (PDF57)
PSY-S14: final Oxford abstract, educational-aspiration assertion
claims.entailment: Main locus-control/bargaining coefficients 0.18/0.21; controlled-appendix 0.16/0.19 with corrected p=.02/.04 and .00/.01. Pooled mobility/aspirations imprecise. Aggregate corrected p=.04/.12 is adjustment-sensitive. Final abstract uses different aspirations wording.
claims.rival: Demand, salience and family-reallocation explanations can produce changed answers without broader norm change. Discontinued behavioural games do not supply the missing discriminator.
claims.lineage: One dataset and same trial across versions; final full tables uninspected, so no silent reconciliation or independent replication credit.

findings.requested_change: Retain documented enrolment/grade/distance and school-sampling limits; recast disability/cycling ability/route applicability as unmeasured rather than established exclusion.
findings.does_not_require: Changing package effect estimates or claiming all girls are represented.

findings.title: Known manuscript/final-abstract aspirations difference
findings.requested_change: Explicitly attribute detailed null/imprecise result to 7 May 2025 manuscript, record final abstract says educational aspirations improved, and preserve unresolved final-table/pooling/outcome-definition check.
findings.does_not_require: Inferring a changed final pooled effect or discarding inspected manuscript estimates.
